Kawal Singh) Challan No.2016/2023 Cnr No.Dlst-02-027234-2023 Judgment Municipal Corporation Of Delhi ......... Complainant Versus M/S Apollo Pharmacy Shop No.5 & 6, E Block Market, Vasant Vihar, New Delhi. .............. Accused Offence punishable under Section - 417 re
texts.facts: . By way of the present Judgment, this court shall dispose off challan bearing No. 2016/2023, of Apollo Pharmacy located at shop no. 19, Old market, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi dated 05.02.2024 against Mr. Pratap C Reddy (Authorized Representative of Apollo pharmacy), under section-417 of Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 (hereinafter referred to as "DMC Act"). BRIEF FACTS: 2. It is alleged against the accused that the pharmacy shop namely, Apollo Pharmacy located at shop no. 5 & 6, E-block market, Vasant Vihar, New Delhi was found being running without a valid MCD Health Trade License (HTL) within the jurisdiction of South district in contravention of the DMC Act, thereby accused has committed the offence punishable under Section-417 read with section-461 of DMC Act. 3. It is pertinent to mention here that the cognizance of the offence had already been taken by this court on 20.12.2023 and a fine was proposed for the summary disposal of the case under the DMC Act. The Authorised Representative (AR) of the accused exercised the option to contest the present challan and accordingly the same is being taken up for adjudication as per law. Mcd vs M/S Apollo Pharmacy-2409 on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100581925/ 1 PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THE COURT: 4. The Authorized Representative (AR) of the accused entered his first appearance on 20.02.2024. Notice under section-251 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) was framed against the accused on the same day, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. It was the defence of the accused that the shop trade in pharmaceutical items and is being run, after taking a valid license from the Drug Control Department as per the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. Therefore, no license from the MCD is required to run the said pharmaceutical shop and he is not liable to pay any fine for not having any license under the DMC Act. 5. Summons were issued to the relevant officer on behalf of the MCD South Branch, and Licensing Health Inspector entered appearance before this court who was examined by this court as PW-1. The witness PW-1 placed on record few photographs of the shop in question as Ex.PW1/B and circular no.PA/MHO-I/MCD/2022/97 dated 07.07.2022 as Ex.PW1/C with respect to the present challan. Opportunity was granted to cross examine PW1 and the same was cross examined by the counsel for the accused. 6. After cross-examination the prosecution closed its evidence and then statement of the AR of the accused under section-313 of Cr.P.C was recorded, wherein he denied all the incriminating evidence and the allegations of the prosecution. He stated that the shop in question is being run by the company i.e., M/S Apollo Pharmacies Ltd after obtaining a valid license from the Drug Control Department under Drugs and cosmetics Act, 1940 and from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). He further stated that no HTL is required to run the shop in question from the MCD thus, he has no liability in the present challan. Further, he chose not to lead any defence evidence to that effect. APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE LED BEFORE THIS COURT:
texts.arguments: 8. Before delving into the facts placed before this court, it is necessary to reiterate the legal provisions. Section-417 of the DMC Act, 1957 states as follows: 417.Premises not to be used for certain purposes without licence (1) No person shall use or permit to be used any premises for any of the following purposes without or otherwise than in conformity with the terms of a licence granted by the Commissioner in this behalf namely: (a) any of the purposes specified in Part I of the Eleventh Schedule; Mcd vs M/S Apollo Pharmacy-2409 on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100581925/ 2 (b) any purpose which is, in the opinion of the Commissioner dangerous to life, health or property or likely to create a nuisance, (c) keeping horses. cattle or other quadruped animals or birds for transportation, sale or hire or for sale of the produce thereof: or (d) storing any of the articles specified in Part II of the Eleventh Schedule except for domestic use of any of those articles: Provided that the corporation may declare that premises in which the aggregate quantity of articles stored for sale does not exceed such quantity as may be prescribed by bye-laws in respect of any such articles shall be exempted from the operation of clause (d). (2) In prescribing the terms of a licence granted under this section for the use of premises as mills or iron yards or for similar purposes the Commissioner may. The counsel for the accused further stated that the shop is being run after taking a valid license from the Drug Control Department under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act as well as from FSSAI. The counsel argued that as per Section-417 of DMC Act the accused is not required to get any license from the MCD since the pharmaceutical items falls under entry-21 of the Eleventh Schedule, which does not mentions sale or trade as one of the necessary criteria for obtaining licence. The second argument of the accused is that as per the proviso of section-417 the accused is given liberty to sell small quantity of cosmetics and food products thus, the provisions of the said section have not been violated by the accused person. The counsel for the accused has relied on a judgment pronounced by this court titled as SDMC vs M/S Apollo Hospital Enterprises Ltd. MCD Challan No. 36580 dated 22.08.2015 in support of his arguments. The issue whether trade of all the purposes mentioned in entry-21 in the Part-1 of the Eleventh Schedule is prohibited or not without obtaining a valid license from the Commissioner was discussed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Sumitra Devi Malik vs MCD & Anr. 1998 (47) DRJ 19. The relevant paragraph is being reproduced as follows: "A perusal of entry No.21 also shows that it is only manufacturing, packing, pressing and the processing in respect of the articles, which is prohibited without licence and not the trading in the items. The Hon'ble Delhi High Court in M/S North Eastern Carrying Corporation vs Municipal Corporation of Delhi W.P(C) No. 5294/1999 decided on 20.04.2010 had observed that "sub-section (3) of Section-417 of DMC Act, 1957 is wholly independent part of Section-417 and even on assuming the requirement of payment of license fee is illegal, the same will not mean that the requirement of a licence also is automatically done away with." 14.
